extraction.Name: Louise Melda Rose—nee Young
extraction.Refused/Protested: she did not desire this patent in fee, as she did not want to pay taxes; that it was sent to her in the mail, and, as she understood that it would be assessed for taxes if she did not take the patent, for which it would later be sold, she accepted the patent
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: in 1919, she traded her 160 acre allotment to her brother, Walter Young, for 80 acres of the home place, which Walter then owned, exchanging deeds, and Walter paying the taxes on her quarter of land
extraction.Buyer: Walter Young (her brother), in exchange for 80 acres of the home place and Walter paying the taxes on her quarter of land
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: she did not sell her place for any debts incurred prior to receiving the patent in fee
extraction.Occupation/Income: her husband, who has poor health, supports the family by farming on heirship land, this being their only source of income
extraction.NOTES: Allotment described as NE¼, Sec. 17, Tp. 37N., R. 36W., of the 6th P.M.; 160 acre allotment; mentally competent; health is not very good; mother of two small children; husband has poor health; she considers she received only about half of what her place was worth but traded to help her brother who was suffering financial reverses; has never received any aid from the County, State nor the United States Government; affidavit sworn April 22, 1929
